title: Feedback of every kind, tied to the version that wrote what was judged; an edit becomes the example's reply
request: Phase 1's feedback gap: a thumb existed on Home's replies, but nothing kept a score, a correction, a person's own version of a reply, an override, or which version of the agent wrote what was judged. A thumb should create the event with the message's version; an edited reply should become a conversation row whose label is the edit; adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.feedback (kinds, targets, check, verdict); feedback.given gains kind, version, score and edited, chat.agent gains message and version (experience contract v7); POST /api/feedback runs the core's check and stamps the version of the message judged; datasets.conversations uses an edit as the reply, a thumb up as the mark and a thumb down as the end of the example; Home gets an edit control, a stage's explanation gets thumbs; the main product's accept, reject and revert of a proposal map to the same kind.
plan: The rules in dclab_core: five kinds, seven targets, one check and one verdict function (an edit beats a rejection beats an approval).
Stamp what wrote a message: the release (library version and a digest of the prompts, tool schemas and validator) on every chat.agent event, with the message's id.
The route resolves the version of the message judged from the log, else the release now.
The conversations builder reads the verdicts; rows carry the label and the originals.
The buttons (Home's edit, stage explanations' thumbs) and the adapter.

decisions.decision: The version is the release (core version and prompts digest) stamped on the chat.agent event, and a thumb inherits the version of the message it judges.
decisions.why: A thumb is about the prompts and rules that wrote the message, not the ones running when the person clicked.

decisions.decision: An edit beats a rejection beats an approval; the newest thumb of a message stands.
decisions.why: A person who turned a reply down and then wrote the better one gave the label; a changed mind is the last thumb.

decisions.decision: A thumb down ends the example before that reply; it does not drop the whole conversation.
decisions.why: What came before was accepted; what the person rejected is not taught, and nothing after it follows from it.

decisions.decision: The original reply stays in edits, never in messages.
decisions.why: A set that trains on the edit must not also hold the text the person replaced.

decisions.decision: The experience event moves to v7 for the new fields.
decisions.why: The rule since 23.2: a kind's fields are part of the contract's shape.

change: dclab_core feedback.py (new), experience.py (fields, v7), datasets.py (conversations), adapters/main_product_experience.py (feedback_events), CHANGELOG 0.43.0, schemas; dclab_rnd experience/__init__.py (release), experience/hooks.py (message and version on chat.agent), agentic/pages/ledger.py (the route), web home.html and core.js (the buttons); tests test_feedback.py (new), the version pins; CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan.

findings.defect: The old route dropped a ref shorter than six characters, so a Home message id like m1 was never in the event.
findings.scenario: on was 'answer' with no id: a thumb could not be joined to its message.
findings.cause: One ID pattern for decisions and messages.
findings.fix: The core's check accepts an id's shape of 1 to 80 characters.

findings.defect: Two assertions of the new test were wrong about the example's length and about which events an export keeps.
findings.scenario: A conversation has the problem, two agent replies and an answer: five messages with the system line; an event with no project follows the workspace's switch.
findings.cause: The test was written from memory of the builder.
findings.fix: The assertions say what the builder and the export do, and the export test shows the redaction.

findings.defect: The export redacted the message ids, so an edit or a thumb hit the wrong message once a set was built.
findings.scenario: Home message ids are m plus ten hex characters; the redaction reads about 99% of them as ids and writes [ID]: every message shared one bucket, so an edit of the second reply replaced both, a thumb down on the second dropped the whole conversation, and the version was lost.
findings.cause: _scrub runs on every payload field, meta included; the tests used ids (m1, m2) that survive it and never went through the export.
findings.fix: The fields the server makes itself (chat.agent message and version, feedback version and target) are exempt when they are an id's shape; a test runs real-shaped ids through export_events and the builder.

findings.defect: Any signed-in role could write training labels: a Business viewer's edit became the example's reply.
findings.scenario: A viewer posts an edited_output for someone else's draft; stamped at the workspace's level, it leaves in the next make datasets.
findings.cause: POST /api/feedback is open to every role (a thumb used to be a record only); now a thumb or an edit changes a set.
findings.fix: The event carries the person's role; a viewer's feedback is recorded and ignored by verdict(), and a viewer's edit is refused with 403.

findings.defect: A message whose version could not be found was stamped with today's release, claiming prompts that did not write it; a failed fingerprint was cached as 'none' for the process.
findings.scenario: A message from before the stamp, a note, or an unreadable log.
findings.cause: A fallback to the release now.
findings.fix: No version when it cannot be found; release() returns 'prompts-unknown' and does not remember a failure.

findings.defect: A rating that was a list or a dict gave a 500; an override of a decision neither checked it nor existed.
findings.cause: A dict lookup with an unchecked value.
findings.fix: A rating must be a string; an override of a decision looks the decision up (404) without making a label.

findings.defect: edits[].index did not point into the final messages when consecutive agent replies were merged.
findings.scenario: Two agent replies in a row become one turn; the edit's index was where the pre-merge position was.
findings.cause: The index was computed before the merge.
findings.fix: The index is the turn the message ended up in.

findings.defect: The edit box said saved when the route had recorded nothing.
findings.scenario: The contract refused a credential-shaped edit; the route answered recorded false with 200.
findings.cause: The page did not read the answer.
findings.fix: The page throws when recorded is false.

findings.defect: The plan said the intern's messages carry the version; they did not.
findings.scenario: A future thumb on an intern answer would fall back.
findings.cause: A claim written before the code.
findings.fix: The intern's answers carry the release; the status says they have no message id yet.

outcome: A thumb, a score, a correction, an edited reply or an override is one event with the version of what was judged; an edit is the reply of the example it came from. Reviewed: 7 findings fixed. The experience event moved once, to v7, for 23.6 and 23.7 together.
lessons: Stamp the producer's version on what it writes, so feedback can inherit it later; the click happens under a different release.
risks: The release is the whole prompt set's digest: any prompt change makes every earlier message a different version, which is the point, but a finer version per purpose would let an edit be traced to one prompt.
The intern's own chat page has no buttons yet; its messages carry the version already.
